title: Polestar x Dutch Design Week: Rethinking materials with Maria Uggla
summary: Maria Uggla, Head of C&M Design at Polestar, shares how design can be a force for progress and why our partnership with Dutch Design Week is a key step forward.
body_markdown:
## From flax to finish


But how does this work in practice? We asked Maria for a concrete example. “Bcomp,” she replied without hesitation.


Developing new materials means balancing long-term research with the requirements of cars in production today. Designers need materials that can be sourced, manufactured and used at scale. That challenge helped bring Polestar and Bcomp together.


Founded in Switzerland in 2011, Bcomp develops high-performance flax-fibre reinforcement fabrics. Its early work in the skiing industry was followed by a partnership with Polestar.


At first, the material’s raw appearance didn’t suit the finish Polestar’s designers wanted. The team began experimenting with the weave, exploring how it could become a visible part of the interior.


Through extensive trial and error, a new weave design emerged. It offered an alternative to traditional expressions of luxury such as leather and veneered wood. “There are enormous possibilities in exploring and creating new expressions when working with new sustainable materials,” Maria says.


## Room to experiment


Art, like a concept car, provides space to experiment with new materials before they reach production. Polestar explored Bcomp’s flax-based composites in the Precept concept car. The material also featured in[We Harvest Wind](https://media.polestar.com/releases/240?lang=ww_WW) , an installation created with ecological artist Thijs Biersteker.


Both projects helped inform the[Polestar Signature Weave](https://www.polestar.com/global/news/polestar-bcomp-the-making-of-our-signature-interior-weave/) , which has since found its way into Polestar 5.
